title: Performance Profiling
concept: Profile XIOM programs and the compiler itself — find hot paths, measure performance, and identify optimization opportunities.
why: You can't optimize what you can't measure. Profiling reveals WHERE time is spent, transforming guesses into data-driven optimization decisions.
theory:
## Measuring What Matters

### Profiling Tools

| Tool | Platform | Use |
|------|----------|-----|
| `perf` | Linux | CPU sampling, cache misses |
| `Instruments` | macOS | Time profiler, allocations |
| `VTune` | Win/Linux | Advanced CPU analysis |
| `Valgrind/Callgrind` | Linux | Instruction counting, call graphs |
| `xiom profile` | All | Built-in profiling |

### Built-in Profiling

```sh
# Profile a program
xiom profile ./target/release/myapp

# Profile specific function
xiom profile --fn compute ./target/release/myapp

# Generate flame graph
xiom profile --flamegraph ./target/release/myapp
```

### Reading a Flame Graph

```
main()                           ████████████████████████████
├── parse_config()               ████
├── process_data()               ████████████████
│   ├── validate()               ████
│   └── compute()                ██████████           ← HOT!
│       └── heavy_math()         ██████████
└── write_output()               ████
```

The wider the bar, the more time spent in that function.

### Benchmarking

```xiom
#[bench]
fn bench_sorting(b: &mut Bencher) {
  let data = generate_random_vec(10000);
  b.iter(|| {
    let mut copy = data.clone();
    copy.sort();
  });
}
```

```sh
xiom bench
# sorting                  time:   [2.1 ms 2.3 ms 2.5 ms]
```

### Profiling the Compiler

```sh
# Profile compiler compilation time
xiom profile --compiler src/

# Results show which compiler phase is slowest:
# Lexer:        0.2s  ██
# Parser:       0.5s  █████
# Type Check:   2.1s  █████████████████████
# Borrow Check: 0.8s  ████████
# Codegen:      1.4s  ██████████████
# LLVM:         4.2s  ██████████████████████████████████████
```

### Optimization Loop

```
1. Profile → 2. Identify hot function → 3. Optimize →
4. Benchmark → 5. Profile again → 6. Verify improvement
```
syntax_ref:
# Profiling:
xiom profile ./binary
xiom profile --flamegraph ./binary
xiom profile --compiler src/      # Profile compilation itself

# Benchmarking:
xiom bench
xiom bench --filter "sort"        # Specific benchmark
tips: Always profile before optimizing — your 'slow function' might not be the bottleneck
Flame graphs visualize the call stack — wider bars = more time, taller stacks = deeper calls
Cache misses often matter more than instruction count — use `perf stat` to measure
Profile with realistic data — small test datasets hide performance problems
common_mistakes: Optimizing without profiling — you'll micro-optimize code that runs 1% of the time
Profiling debug builds — debug code has different performance characteristics than release
Ignoring memory allocation overhead — profiling CPU time misses memory pressure issues
